message.abstract: <jats:p>The definition of the generic limits of <jats:italic>Xerocomus</jats:italic> s. l. and particularly the delimitation of this genus from <jats:italic>Boletus</jats:italic> is very unclear and controversial. During his study of European species of the <jats:italic>Boletaceae</jats:italic>, the author has come to the conclusion that <jats:italic>Xerocomus</jats:italic> in a wide concept is a heterogeneous mixture of several groups of species. These groups are separated from each other by different anatomical and some other characters. Also recent molecular studies show that <jats:italic>Xerocomus</jats:italic> s. l. is not a monophyletic group. In agreement with these facts, the European species of <jats:italic>Xerocomus</jats:italic> s. l. whose anatomy was studied by the present author are here classified into the following, more distinctly delimited genera: <jats:italic>Xerocomus</jats:italic> s. str., <jats:italic>Phylloporus</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Xerocomellus</jats:italic> gen. nov., <jats:italic>Hemileccinum</jats:italic> gen. nov. and <jats:italic>Pseudoboletus.Boletus badius</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Boletus moravicus</jats:italic>, also often treated as species of <jats:italic>Xerocomus</jats:italic>, are retained for the present in the genus <jats:italic>Boletus</jats:italic>. The differences between <jats:italic>Xerocomus</jats:italic> s. str., <jats:italic>Phylloporus</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Xerocomellus</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Hemileccinum, Pseudoboletus</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Boletus</jats:italic> (which is related to this group of genera) are discussed in detail. Two new genera, <jats:italic>Xerocomellus</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Hemileccinum,</jats:italic> and necessary new combinations of species names are proposed.</jats:p>
title: Xerocomus s. l. in the light of the present state of knowledge.
